designDecision.fixTaken: (b) -- collapse a multi-layer city (one place_fips, multiple staged city_key base layers) to ONE processCity pass against the UNION of its layers' zone polygons. Taking the dispatch's recommended shape; no reason found not to.
designDecision.whyNotA: (a) intersecting each city_key row's population by its own layer's county coverage would require hardcoding or deriving a city_key-to-county mapping that does not exist as data anywhere in this schema (tx_zoning_district_staging carries bbox columns per polygon, not a declared county per city_key row) -- (b) needs no new mapping at all, reuses the existing per-polygon bbox/geometry the join already has, and the dispatch's own reasoning (sourceUrl already travels per matched polygon) generalizes to a stronger claim: NO per-match field needs a group-level city fallback if the match itself carries its own city_key. Also removes the ORDER BY tie hazard structurally (one row per place_fips now, never two racing to throw).
designDecision.correctnessGapFoundBeyondTheDispatchsExp: The dispatch's own text only asks to confirm sourceUrl survives a union pass. Reading buildZoningCells and its caller shows a SECOND rail cell, zoningJurisdictionKey, is currently written from city.cityKey -- the single, row-level city_key of a single-layer city. A naive union implementation that keeps writing one group-level city_key for every matched parcel would silently write the WRONG jurisdiction key for any parcel matched against the OTHER layer in the union (e.g. a Travis parcel matched via elgin-tx-travis's polygon would get zoningJurisdictionKey='elgin-tx' if the group's representative key were used). This is exactly the class of silent-fallback defect DEV_PROCESS section 2 exists to catch, and it would not be caught by the dispatch's own prescribed check (reading sourceUrl only). Decision: HOIST_ZONES_SQL and CHUNK_ZONE_MATCH_SQL both gain a city_key column carried per-polygon-row (already implicitly true per-row in tx_zoning_district_staging, just not selected today because a single-city_key WHERE made it constant), and buildZoningCells is called with the MATCHED row's own city_key, never the group's. sourceUrl was already correct by the same mechanism (per-matched-row, not group-level) and is unaffected; this generalizes that same correctness property to the sibling field the dispatch did not name.
implementationPlan: IN_SCOPE_CITIES_SQL: GROUP BY place_fips/city_name/in_city_parcels, array_agg(DISTINCT city_key) AS city_keys -- one row per place_fips, not one per (place_fips, city_key). Exclusion filter (NOT city_key = ANY(excluded)) applies before the aggregation, same semantics as today.

loadInScopeCities: city.cityKey (singular) -> city.cityKeys (array). This is a breaking shape change to the function's return type, done deliberately rather than papered over with a fake singular representative, because a fake singular would be the same silent-fallback class named above one level up the call stack.
--city flag matching: a city is selected if ANY of its cityKeys is in the override list (was: single-key equality).
HOIST_ZONES_SQL: WHERE city_key = $1 -> WHERE city_key = ANY($1::text[]); adds city_key to both the decoded CTE and the final SELECT (r5_zones_ok gains a city_key column).
CHUNK_ZONE_MATCH_SQL: r5_zones_ok's city_key threaded through hits/kept/ranked/final SELECT, so each match names which specific staged layer row it came from.

processCity: buildZoningCells({ ..., cityKey: m.city_key, ... }) per match, not city.cityKey. HOIST_ZONES_SQL invoked with city.cityKeys (array). Result object's cityKey field -> cityKeys (array), mirroring the input shape.
